headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Test for the first time in Darwin
summary: The Tigers end a 23-year wait to secure a nine-wicket victory, described by Mark Waugh as potentially the biggest upset in Australian cricket history.
details: Bangladesh secured a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.
The triumph ends a 23-year wait for the Tigers to play a Test match in Australia, and was achieved in just four days.
Former Australian batter Mark Waugh called the result "potentially the biggest upset I can remember in Australia," comparing it to the West Indies' victory at the Gabba.
The victory was even more remarkable as Bangladesh played without their top two bowlers, Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam, against a full-strength Australian side.
Despite being bowled out for 54 in a tour match against a Cricket Australia XI, the Tigers bounced back by bowling Australia out for 198 on the opening day.
Bangladesh then scored 426, building a massive lead that led to the victory on the fourth day.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, praising the team's achievement as a landmark victory for the country.
caption:
A 23-year wait is over! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh has just secured its first-ever Test win in Australia, and even the Australian legends are calling it one of the biggest upsets ever.

Bangladesh secured a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.

The triumph ends a 23-year wait for the Tigers to play a Test match in Australia, and was achieved in just four days.

Former Australian batter Mark Waugh called the result "potentially the biggest upset I can remember in Australia," comparing it to the West Indies' victory at the Gabba.

The victory was even more remarkable as Bangladesh played without their top two bowlers, Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam, against a full-strength Australian side.

Despite being bowled out for 54 in a tour match against a Cricket Australia XI, the Tigers bounced back by bowling Australia out for 198 on the opening day.

Bangladesh then scored 426, building a massive lead that led to the victory on the fourth day.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, praising the team's achievement as a landmark victory for the country.

headline_marked: EC [[validates nominations of Mirza Fakhrul and Oli Ahmed]] for presidential poll
headline: EC validates nominations of Mirza Fakhrul and Oli Ahmed for presidential poll
summary: The Election Commission has cleared the nomination papers of both candidates after a scrutiny process on Sunday.
details: The Election Commission (EC) has declared the nomination papers of presidential candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as valid.
Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin conducted the scrutiny of the nomination papers at the EC building on Sunday afternoon.
The nomination was validated after no discrepancies were found during the verification process.
Earlier, the nomination of Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, the presidential candidate of the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, was also declared valid.
The 23rd presidential election is scheduled to take place on August 20.
The deadline for withdrawing candidacy is 4:00 PM on August 18.
caption:
Two major presidential candidates have just cleared the EC's scrutiny process.

The Election Commission (EC) has declared the nomination papers of presidential candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as valid.

Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin conducted the scrutiny of the nomination papers at the EC building on Sunday afternoon.

The nomination was validated after no discrepancies were found during the verification process.

Earlier, the nomination of Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, the presidential candidate of the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, was also declared valid.

The 23rd presidential election is scheduled to take place on August 20.

The deadline for withdrawing candidacy is 4:00 PM on August 18.
